subject: Hybrid embedding / generation billing — proration, quantum, and minimums
messages:
From: Alyssa Greene <alyssa@devdocs.io>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: pricing@devdocs.io
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hybrid embedding / generation billing — quick question

Hi Karthik,

Quick one from our infra/finance team — we generate embeddings for most calls (api/embeddings) and occasionally run generation that uses those embeddings as context. A couple of specific asks:

- When we produce embeddings (separate embedding API calls) and then use them as input to a generation request, are those embedding tokens charged only at the embedding rate (when generated), or do they also contribute to the generation request's input token count (and any per-call minimums/rounding there)?
- What rounding/quantum rules apply for small embedding calls? We have lots of tiny embedding calls (50–200 embedding units) batched by our service every minute — are those rounded per-call, per-minute, or smoothed at invoice time?
- Example: on an average day we do ~1.2M embedding units (50-unit calls) and maybe 10k generation tokens across 200 generation requests. How should we expect our monthly invoice to look in terms of minimums and rounding?

I've attached a tiny sample usage export (sample-usage.csv) to illustrate. Can you point us to the precise rules so we can model cost? Also if there are pilot concessions for embedding-heavy startups, we'd love to understand that.

Thanks,
Alyssa
Alyssa Greene
Head of Platform, DevDocs Inc
alyssa@devdocs.io

[attachment: sample-usage.csv]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Greene <alyssa@devdocs.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, pricing@devdocs.io
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hybrid embedding / generation billing — quick question

Hi Alyssa — thanks for the clear examples and the CSV, that helped. TL;DR answers first, then worked examples.

Short answers:
- If you call /embeddings as a separate API call, those charges are billed against the embeddings SKU (per-embedding-unit). Those embedding calls do NOT also get counted again as input tokens for generation unless you pass the embedding content inline in the same generation request.
- If you serialize embeddings into a generation request (i.e., you include raw tokenized text or embedding vectors inline in the prompt payload), the tokens/bytes in that generation request are counted toward the generation input and subject to generation rounding/quantum.
- Rounding/quantum: embeddings are billed in 100-embedding-unit quanta for invoice discretization; generation tokens are billed in 10-token quanta for per-call minimums. We also apply monthly smoothing for committed customers (see examples).

Worked examples (using your numbers):
1) Your current flow: separate embedding calls (1.2M embedding units) + generation that references stored embedding IDs (200 generation requests, 10k gen tokens total).
   - Embeddings: 1.2M embedding units billed at embedding unit price, rounded up to nearest 100-unit quantum. So line item = ceil(1,200,000 / 100) * 100 = 1,200,000 (no extra rounding in this aggregate example, but small per-call rounding can add up if you create many individual 50-unit calls).
   - Generation: 10k tokens billed at generation per-token price, rounded per-call to 10-token quanta. If each of the 200 requests is small (avg 50 tokens), each request will be rounded to the nearest 10 tokens before summing. Summation example: avg 50 -> no extra rounding overhead in aggregate, but if you had many 1–9 token calls they'd round up to 10.
   - Because the embedding generation and the later generation request are separate API calls and use stored embedding IDs, we do NOT double-bill the same content.

2) Alternative flow: if you were to embed on-the-fly and inline the resulting vector/text into the generation request payload (single combined request):
   - We treat that as a generation request for billing purposes. The serialized input that contains the embedding (or its textual provenance) counts as input tokens, so it would be subject to generation token quantum (10-token) as well as any minimum per-generation call. We would not, in that single-call case, also bill the embedding SKU separately — it becomes part of the generation request.

3) Small-call smoothing and pilot credits:
   - For pay-as-you-go customers, per-call rounding occurs at request time and can aggregate to a ~1–5% effective uplift depending on call size distribution.
   - For customers on a monthly committed plan (or pilots where we agree to smoothing), we can apply invoice-level smoothing: we calculate total raw units and apply quantum rounding at the invoice line level instead of per-API-call. That typically reduces the rounding overhead dramatically for high-cardinality small calls.

A couple of follow-ups that would help us give an exact model:
- Are the 50–200 "embedding units" in your sample actual embedding-charge units (i.e., the unit returned in our embeddings response) or are they tokens before embedding?
- Do you batch multiple embedding calls into one API call from your client, or are they separate HTTP requests?

If you want, we can run a quick invoice-model from your sample CSV and show the delta between per-call rounding vs invoice-level smoothing. Happy to do that and to surface pilot concession options.

Best,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Hybrid embedding / generation billing — quick question

Thanks Karthik — super helpful. A few clarifications after digging in with infra:

- The 50–200 numbers in sample-usage.csv are the embedding-unit counts returned after calling /embeddings (so yes, embedding-charge units). They are emitted as separate HTTP requests from our worker tier (each event is its own call).
- We store embeddings (by id) in our vector store and generation requests reference those ids via metadata — we do not serialize raw vectors into the generation payload.

So sounds like the two best levers are: 1) batch embeddings at our side to reduce per-call rounding, or 2) ask Redwood for invoice-level smoothing for the pilot window. Can you outline what smoothing looks like for a pilot (math and any contract language)? Also, is there a minimum commit to qualify?

Appreciate the rapid response — if you can run the sample CSV through invoice-level smoothing that would be great.

—Alyssa

Hi Alyssa — looping in Neha from our pricing/finance team to finalize. Appreciate the detail here.

Neha and I discussed a pilot concession we can offer to DevDocs Inc to reduce the short-term impact of per-call rounding while we validate cost behavior:

- Pilot term: 90 days from start date.
- Embedding unit price: standard list price, with a temporary 10% volume discount applied to all embedding usage up to 250M units during the pilot period.
- Rounding/smoothing: for the pilot we will apply invoice-level smoothing for the embedding line (we will sum raw embedding units for the invoice period and round the final line to the 100-unit quantum rather than applying per-request rounding). That will remove most micro-call uplift.
- Minimums: we will waive embedding per-call minimums for calls that are sent to your "worker-batch" gateway (the gateway signature in the CSV) for the pilot. This requires enabling a gateway header to identify batched worker calls so our billing pipeline can exclude per-request quantum on those hits.
- Ops/process: we'll share a contract addendum and a short onboarding checklist (we need the gateway header and monthly usage export).

I've attached a draft concession addendum (contract-draft-v2.docx) — Neha, please confirm the exact billing language (I pulled preliminary text below).

If this works, next steps: Alyssa signs the addendum, we enable invoice-level smoothing for DevDocs account, and we run a 30-day lookback to project expected invoices.

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call to walk through examples.
